scope: Actual generated Prisma client and PostgreSQL; real signed JWTs, Express loopback HTTP middleware. Signing/database outage ports explicitly controlled in named checks. No full server/browser/provider/financial or production proof.
checks: Actual bcrypt/database login denies incorrect password
Actual bcrypt login persists last-login and issues a signed token resolved to its current principal
Six real PostgreSQL rotations issue one successor and atomically link the consumed predecessor
Repeated consumed token cannot create another database successor
Actual HTTP guard replaces stale founder claims with current database role
Disabling an actual database account immediately denies existing access and refresh
Mandatory and optional anonymous HTTP behavior preserved
A correctly signed JWT without expiry is rejected
Actual SQL successor failure rolls back predecessor consumption and linkage
Original refresh remains usable after rolled-back database failure
Controlled signing failure also rolls back real PostgreSQL successor and predecessor
Actual HTTP guards fail closed on a controlled database-port failure without exposing its details
Revoked refresh token cannot create a successor
Test-owned SQL failure trigger cleaned up
